title: Overnight cron pipeline with morning branch review workflow
problem: Pipeline runs are expensive when supervised live from a parent session - the parent's 1M context burns cache reads on every turn while stages run, on top of the captured pipeline-* stage costs. There is no way to batch pipeline work into low-attention hours and review results efficiently the next day. Manually firing pipeline runs from a session also means usage is consumed during peak hours when it is most needed for interactive work.
description:
Goal: pipeline runs happen unattended overnight, leave their work as open branches, and a single morning session reviews and merges what is good.

Why this shape:
- Removes parent-session supervision overhead, which is likely the single biggest hidden cost of pipeline runs (parent's 1M context cache reads dwarf stage tokens).
- 'Branch open, not merged' is a natural approval gate - no pipeline/approval.py pause logic needed.
- Failed runs are cheap to discard (close branch).
- Morning review session is mostly reading diffs (cheap turns) instead of generating (expensive turns), giving better cache utilization.
- Pattern already exists informally - see scribe note #146 'PIPELINE PENDING REVIEW: Orchestrator test. Branch pipeline/9173fa8a...' - this ticket formalizes it.

Components to build / wire:
1. Cron trigger (use existing schedule skill / RemoteTrigger infra). Fires N times per night, each invocation drains one backlog item.
2. Orchestrator 'detached' mode: runs all stages, commits to a branch, stops. Does NOT merge. Does NOT push by default (decide whether to push or leave local).
3. Hard per-run token cap. Non-negotiable. A runaway stage at 3am with no human can drain a day's budget. Wire to existing round_counter / file_count guardrails or add a token-budget guardrail if missing.
4. Backlog picker: simplest viable - first-come-first-served from pipeline/backlog/*.json in slug order, or oldest-mtime first. Skip items already in progress (have an open branch).
5. Branch naming + listing: confirm existing convention (pipeline/<slug>-<short-uuid> looks right from note #146). Add pipeline/queue.py or similar that lists 'ready for review' branches with their source tickets, status, token cost, and a one-line summary scraped from the ticket.
6. Pre-fire hygiene check: cron skips if more than N unreviewed pipeline branches exist (configurable, default ~5). Prevents pile-up.
7. Logging: each cron run writes a structured log (start time, ticket picked, stages completed, total tokens, exit status, branch name) to a known location for morning triage.

Open questions:
- Push branches to remote or keep local? Remote = visible from anywhere but adds noise to GitHub. Local = clean but tied to one machine (and conflicts with the portability epic).
- Should the morning review session itself be a skill / slash command (e.g. /review-pipeline-queue) that lists branches, lets you pick one, walks the diff, merges or discards?
- Sequencing vs parallelism: v1 sequential to avoid conflicts, but if backlog is big and items are unrelated, parallel might be worth revisiting.
- Token cap value: what number actually protects budget without killing legitimate large refactors? Needs a calibration pass against existing pipeline run history.

Definition of done: a cron job runs N pipeline backlog items overnight, leaves N branches in a known state, and a morning command lists them with enough info to decide which to merge. Token budget for the entire night is bounded and logged.
scope: cron/scheduled trigger that drains pipeline/backlog, orchestrator mode that stops at 'branch ready for review' instead of merging, hard per-run token cap, queue listing tool for morning review (e.g. pipeline/queue.py), branch naming convention (likely already exists), hygiene check that skips cron if too many unreviewed branches exist. Out of scope: parallel run conflict resolution (sequential v1), automatic merging, autonomous PR creation.
